source_text: Πάλιν ὢ τῆς δυσσεβοῦς κρίσεως. Μετὰ τὸ τελειωθῆναι τοὺς ἁγίους τοῦ Χριστοῦ μάρτυρας Παπίαν, Διόδωρον καὶ Κλαυδιανὸν ἐπεβέβηκεν ὁ ἡγεμὼν τῇ πόλει Μαγυδῷ, καὶ καθίσας ἐν τῷ προαστείῳ τοῦ Διὸς ἐπειρᾶτο κἀκεῖσε τοὺς οἰκήτορας διὰ τοῦ κήρυκος προσκαλεῖσθαι. Οἱ δὲ τῆς κηρυκῆς τοῦ βοῶντος ἐπακούσαντες μᾶλλον σπουδαιοτέρως ὑπεχώρησαν ἐκ τῆς πόλεως πάντα καταλείψαντες, ὥστε τὴν πόλιν μόνην ὑπολειφθῆναι μετὰ τοῦ μιαροῦ ἄρχοντος καὶ τῆς τάξεως αὐτοῦ. Ὁ δὲ ἐπέστειλεν σιγγουλαρίους καί τινας ἄλλους κύκλῳ τῆς πόλεως ἀναζητεῖν πανταχοῦ καὶ κατ᾽ οἶκον, εἴ τινας εὕροιεν. Ἦλθον οἱ ἀποσταλέντες καὶ ἀπήγγειλαν αὐτῷ μηδένα εὑρηκέναι ἐν τῇ πόλει ἢ ἐν τοῖς ἀγροῖς.
pass_a_gloss: Again — O the impious judgment. After Papian, Diodorus and Claudian, the holy martyrs of Christ, were brought to completion, the governor advanced upon the city Magydus, and having seated himself in the suburb belonging to Zeus he attempted also there to summon the inhabitants through the herald. But those who heard the cry of the proclaiming voice withdrew from the city even more zealously, leaving all things behind, so that the city was left alone together with the defiled ruler and his staff. And he sent out singularii and certain others in a circuit of the city to seek everywhere and by house, if they might find anyone. The men sent came and announced to him that they had found no one in the city or in the fields.
pass_b_english: Once more — O the impious verdict! After Christ's holy martyrs Papian, Diodorus, and Claudian had completed their course, the governor marched upon the city of Magydus, and taking his seat in the suburb of Zeus he tried to summon the inhabitants there also by the herald. Yet those who heard the shouting voice of the proclamation withdrew from the city with still greater eagerness, abandoning everything, so that the city was left desolate with only the polluted magistrate and his retinue.

So he dispatched the singularii and certain others to search round about the city, everywhere and from house to house, in case they might find anyone. The men who had been sent came and reported back to him that they had found no one, neither in the city nor in the fields.

lemmas.gloss: to be brought to completion, here to die as martyrs

choices.why: aorist passive infinitive after μετὰ τό marks the completed event of martyrdom, not ordinary finishing
μιαρός is moral-religious defilement in a martyrdom context, characterizing the persecutor rather than merely unfair
